# Extensions — Study 06 (Clockwork-Vol): the beat-7 rescues, worked

*Generated by [`examples/verify_extensions.py`](../examples/verify_extensions.py). Real
cached VIX/SPX, as-of **2026-06-01**, VIX fingerprint **`6c2029b57135`** (9,171 sessions. Each row is one
change to the baseline adaptive cycle; `dir_skill` is the walk-forward next-20-session
direction hit rate (0.50 = a coin), `*_p` are p-values against the random-phase null,
`trade_*` is the long-S&P-when-vol-projected-to-fall expression.*

## 1 · Do the rescues revive the VIX cycle?
```
                              dir_skill  skill_p  trade_sharpe  trade_p  exposure  max_dd
variant                                                                                  
baseline (adaptive re-tune)      0.4946   0.7405        0.3313   0.7413    0.5931 -0.3410
fixed 80d (tweet VIX clock)      0.5327   0.0379        0.6414   0.1294    0.5014 -0.4140
fixed 40d (tweet VIX clock)      0.4970   0.5230        0.3724   0.4876    0.4980 -0.3897
amplitude-gated (amp ≥ 0.5σ)     0.4946   0.7405           NaN   0.0050    0.0000  0.0000
```

- **Hard-wiring 40d does nothing; hard-wiring 80d flickers — but fragilely.** Fixing the
  tweet's literal 40-day clock leaves the forecast a coin flip (skill ≈ 0.497, p ≈ 0.52).
  Fixing the **80-day** clock gives a *marginal* tick — direction skill **0.533, p ≈ 0.04**
  against the random-phase null — the one number in the whole study that even approaches
  significance. It does **not** survive scrutiny: (i) it is a **single hand-picked period**
  with no correction for having tried several, (ii) it directly **contradicts the spectral
  test**, where 80-day power sits *inside* the red-noise envelope (p ≈ 0.9995 — there is no
  peak there to forecast from), and (iii) it does **not** carry into a significant trade
  (Sharpe 0.64 but p ≈ 0.13 vs the null, and barely above buy-and-hold's 0.56 on 50%
  exposure). This is the textbook **"significant raw, fragile to method and selection"** —
  a `WEAK` fragment, not a clock.
- **The amplitude gate never even fires.** Requiring the in-sample cycle amplitude to reach
  0.5σ of the level zeroes the position *every day*: the cyclical component is always small
  next to the VIX's own variance. That is itself the verdict in miniature — there is no
  window in 36 years where a "strong, clear cycle" is present to trade.

## 2 · Is the cycle in *stocks* instead? The S&P's own clocks
*The tweet ties the VIX cycle to a stock 20-week (~100d) and 4-year (~1000d) cycle. Tested
directly on log-S&P against AR(1) red noise:*
```
               data_peak_power  p_value
target_period                          
100.0000                0.1298   1.0000
250.0000                0.7065   1.0000
1,000.0000             11.4089   0.9995
```

- None of the named stock clocks clears the red-noise envelope either. The 4-year peak is the
  closest to interesting, but a sample with only a handful of 4-year spans can't separate a
  "cycle" from low-frequency red noise — exactly the trap the test is built to catch.
